etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Anglo-Norman resemblance, from Old French (compare French ressemblance).

Morphologically resemble +‎ -ance.

definitions.definition: The quality or state of resembling.

quote.citation: 1838 (date written), L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], “(please specify the page)”, in Lady Anne Granard; or, Keeping up Appearances. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], published 1842, →OCLC, pages 16–17:
quote.text: His wife and sister had too many points of resemblance, not to entertain a strong and mutual dislike.

definitions.definition: That which resembles, or is similar; a representation; a likeness.
